Hierarchical response clustering

Branch geometry uses Ward D2 on all retained standardized, equally block-weighted coordinates. Coloured circles identify statistical groups at the chosen cut. Regime tiles use the separate value-added rule; hover or focus them for signed responses. Regime colours follow the tree’s first split: warm colours (FIC, CD) are the EU-gains/RoW-loses regimes, cool colours (PL, then the two SC branches) the rest. In the 96-observation tree the first branch holds every configuration of Sc2 HH-Energy, Sc10 Int-Metal and Sc13 Int-Energy; in the 12-profile tree it holds Sc10 Int-Metal and Sc13 Int-Energy, and Sc2 HH-Energy joins the other branch. Built on one regional setup at a time, the trees differ: on EU/RoW alone the first branch is exactly Sc2 HH-Energy, Sc10 Int-Metal and Sc13 Int-Energy, the three FIC/CD scenarios; on North/South alone Sc1 HH-Food splits off first.

Select a named leaf or regime tile to inspect it. Highlighting preserves the full hierarchy.

How well supported is this cut?

Left: each bar spans the range of Ward merge heights over which the tree has exactly k groups; a cut is robust when its bar is long and fragile when it is short. Right: mean silhouette by k. A leaf’s silhouette is (b − a)/max(a, b), where a is its mean distance to its own group and b to the nearest other group; it runs from −1 (closer to another group) to +1, and a leaf alone in its group scores 0 by convention. Kaufman and Rousseeuw read a mean of 0.26–0.50 as weak structure and 0.51–0.70 as reasonable. The per-leaf silhouette is drawn beside each leaf in the tree above.

Principal component analysis

Point colour and outlined ovals (labelled G1, G2, …) show Ward groups; shaded borderless ovals (labelled in italics) show the separate value-added regimes, in a different palette. Each oval encloses its observations in this two-dimensional projection; it is not a confidence region. Ovals can overlap because the clustering uses more than two coordinates. The notes report each Ward group’s regime mix.

    Regimes across closures

    Rows follow the leaf order of the twelve-profile Ward tree in the Hierarchy tab. Gold, fiat and quasi-float retain the same broad labels within each setup. OPENFIXG changes six EU/RoW labels and one North/South label; North/South Int-Wood also changes SCc to SCw. SCw can include expansion: it requires a weak region-2 response, irrespective of region-1 sign.

    Scenario, setup and closure effects

    Descriptive shares across 96 deterministic experiments: twelve scenarios, two regional setups and four closures, with six equally weighted outcome blocks. The full factorial has no residual degrees of freedom; these are not inferential significance tests.

    Signed response magnitudes

    Display bands in each coordinate’s reported units: +₀/−₀ = nonzero magnitude below 0.003; +/− = 0.003–0.03; ++/−− = 0.03–0.3; +++/−−− = at least 0.3. Exact zero = 0. These display bands do not assign regimes. Hover a cell for its numerical response and units.
